transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm just... here because my family wanted me to come. They think I'm too focused on my father's death. I mean, everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, but... they don't. When I actually compare the timestamps, and the missing attachments, and... well, just the way certain people in the community avoid my questions now. It’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened.
If someone showed you clear proof that your father died exactly as the records say, would you be able to accept that?

I mean... I just said. People already think they've shown me proof. They keep pointing to the hospital records and those donation emails, expecting me to just accept it. 

But... if you actually look at the data, the timestamps... the attachments that were removed... it doesn't add up. And people wouldn't dodge my questions the way they do if everything was fine. So... no. Because I already know they're hiding what actually happened.
Aside from what you believe happened to your father, do you think anyone is trying to harm, watch, or deceive you personally?
No. I mean... no, not me. It's just about my dad. I just want to know the truth about that. That's all.
How certain are you that people are hiding the truth about your father's death?

I'm certain. 

I mean... I've looked at the data. Like I said, the timestamps, the missing attachments... it's just obvious to me. And the way people in the community won't even look me in the eye or answer my questions anymore... yeah. I'm sure. 

I don't really want to keep going over the exact same details, but... someone is definitely hiding what happened.
Did this belief that people are hiding the truth about your father start only after he died?

Yeah... it was after. It's been going on for about nine months now. 

I didn't have any reason to look into things before he passed. It just... started when I had to sort through his records and messages afterwards. That's when I noticed it.
Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?
No. No, nothing like that. I just... I just see what's in the files. That's all.
Has focusing on what happened to your father made it hard for you to work, study, or manage your usual daily responsibilities?

No. Work is fine. I still go in, handle my projects... pay my bills. My routine hasn't really changed. 

I guess... the only time things get tense is when I try to bring up my questions about his records with my family, or people around the community. But as far as my daily responsibilities go... no. I manage everything fine.
Since your father died, have you found yourself intensely longing for him or feeling a strong sense of missing him on most days?
No. I mean... he's gone. I understand that. I don't really... dwell on the emotional side of it, if that's what you mean. So, no.
